rationale:
structural: The only structural clause is the prescribed signature, `impl<'d, D: Domain> ValidationContext<'d, D> { pub fn read(&self, node: &NodeId<D>) -> Result<D::NodeContent, D::Error>; }`. A `read` taking `NodeId<D>` by value, or returning a different type, would break that signature. `crates/trust-but-verify/src/procedure.rs#impl[ValidationContext<'d, D>]#2/fn[read]` declares exactly that signature and carries the `{impl}` marker. Recording the fingerprint is observable behavior, covered by `read_node.inputs`, which is only cited. Nothing prescribes how it is recorded. `read` delegates to `fn[read_snapshot]` in the same impl, which calls `prepare_read`, then `record_read(*node, snapshot.fingerprint.clone())`, then returns the snapshot. `read` returns `.content`, so a failed read propagates the error through `?` with no recording. No library, algorithm or type is named beyond the signature, and the supplied root covers it.

behavioral: The reviewed tests adequately check `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.ValidationContext.read`. The obligations are to return the node contents and, under `read_node.inputs`, to record the node identity and the fingerprint of the returned contents on success. A failed read must record no observation. A later read with different contents must record a different fingerprint.

- **Success records identity and fingerprint.** `crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph/validation_tests.rs#fn[snapshots_record_exact_reads_and_retain_distinct_versions]` calls `read` on node 1 holding "before". It asserts that the returned contents are "before". It then asserts that `earlier` equals `[Dependency::Node(node1, fp("before"))]`, so the recorded dependency has the right identity and fingerprint.
- **Later change.** The same test changes node 1 to "after" and reads again. It asserts that the contents are "after" and that the dependencies hold both `fp("before")` and `fp("after")` for node 1. The finished record's dependencies match, and `is_current` is false.
- **Failed read.** The same test reads missing node 2 and asserts `is_err`, and the dependency list afterwards is still the two node-1 entries. `fn[direct_reads_return_complete_unicode_contents_and_snapshots]` in the same file asserts the "missing" error on a fresh context and `dependencies().is_empty()`.
- **Returned contents.** `fn[direct_reads_return_complete_unicode_contents_and_snapshots]` covers an empty string and a large multi-byte Unicode string. It asserts that `read` returns contents whose `format()` equals the original, including after the graph content is replaced. It also asserts that the fingerprint matches `fp(original)`.

The agent-delivery paragraph of `read_node.inputs` concerns the harness, not `ValidationContext::read`, so it needs no test here. Staleness reporting belongs to `evidence.checking_records`, a cited requirement whose tests are not reassessed here. `public_exports_match_the_appendix` is unrelated to this behavior.

text: :::{req} ValidationContext.read
Read a graph node and record the fingerprint of the returned contents under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.read_node.inputs`.
```rust,ignore
impl<'d, D: Domain> ValidationContext<'d, D> {
pub fn read(&self, node: &NodeId<D>) -> Result<D::NodeContent, D::Error>;
:::{req} read_node.inputs
A successful `ValidationContext::read` records the node's identity and the
fingerprint of the returned contents, under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.node_inputs`. A failed read records no
successful observation. The evidence becomes stale when a later read of that
node has a different fingerprint; a failure to resolve it is reported by
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.checking_records`.
For a Rust caller, the SDK records the fingerprint when `read` returns the
contents. For an agent, the harness puts a tool result in the next request to
the model and records the fingerprint once the provider responds successfully.
That successful exchange is *delivery*. For example, suppose the tool reads a
function that returns `3`, and someone changes it to return `4` before the
provider responds. The model saw the version that returns `3`, so the SDK
records the fingerprint it computed from that version. Reading the function
again at this point would record a fingerprint for code the model never saw.
